opening_activity: boring a pilot hole into a wooden display base with an old hand-cranked geared drill, then stopping when its exposed interlocking gears bind mid-turn
opening_location: quiet maritime museum exhibit-preparation room beside an unfinished shipwreck display
opening_environment: a practical museum prep space with timber mounts, conservation crates, muted work lamps, and nautical artifacts waiting to be installed
topic_visual_link: The visibly jammed hand-powered gear train echoes the Antikythera mechanism's tightly packed gears and immediately raises the idea that sophisticated mechanical computation can exist without electricity.
opening_visual_proof: In the first seconds, the crone's hand turns the drill crank while two exposed metal gears rotate together, catch abruptly tooth-to-tooth, and freeze the drill bit above the wood.
curiosity_trigger: the crank suddenly resists with a dry metallic click while the meshed gears remain visibly locked
trigger_object: the exposed gear pair of the hand-cranked drill
reaction: She narrows her large eyes at the frozen gears, gives the raven a knowing sideways glance, and tests the crank once more with one long finger.
entry_retrieval: She releases the drill, follows the line of its meshed gears with one pointed finger, then reaches beneath a folded protective cloth on the same work surface and reveals her glass orb; her moss-green sleeve and long fingers remain clearly in frame as she turns it toward the camera.
world_style_hint: submerged Mediterranean archaeology shifting into precise bronze mechanical cutaways, engraved astronomical dials, and luminous orbital geometry
reason: A hand-cranked drill gives the crone a compact, believable task whose suddenly jammed visible gears naturally mirror the ancient mechanism's defining combination of manual power, dense gearing, and unexpected sophistication.
